title_as_printed: Experimental Results of Vapor Pressure Lowering Measurements for Sodium Chloride Solutions

footnotes_as_printed.a: Average value of three experimental results.
footnotes_as_printed.b: Average value of two experimental results.

pressure_note: no pressure column; the authors state the osmotic coefficients are applicable to the solution under a total pressure equal to the vapor pressure of pure water p0 at each temperature (phi at p = p0). The measured quantity is the vapor pressure lowering dp = p0 - p in mm (mercury), corrected to density of Hg at 0 C

P.what: pure-water saturation pressure p0 at T; not printed

value.col: Osmotic coefficient phi at p = p0

value2.what: measured vapour pressure lowering of the solution relative to pure water (raw measurement)

composition.other_species: pure water (triply distilled, degassed); NaCl only

conversion_needs: dp in mm of mercury (density of Hg at 0 C); T in C
notes: Molality is the value at each temperature recalculated by the authors from the initial weight-basis molality, the cell volume, initial liquid volume and steam density. Rows marked a/b are averages of 3 or 2 runs. 'value' follows the osmotic coefficient as the paper's reported result (per task convention) with dp as value2; the primary measurement is dp.
